blocks.h2: When to Call for Drain Cleaning
blocks.body: Call when a plunger doesn't clear it, when the same drain clogs again within a few weeks or when you smell sewer gas from a drain. Pay attention to where it's happening. One slow sink is usually a local clog. If the floor drain backs up when the washer drains, or the tub gurgles when you flush, the main line is involved, and that's a job for [sewer rodding](/arlington-heights/sewer-rodding).

img.alt: Illustration of common signs a drain needs professional cleaning

blocks.h2: Clogged Drain Repair in Arlington Heights
bodies: Most household clogs are made of everyday things: hair and soap in the bathroom, grease and food scraps in the kitchen, lint in the laundry line. We clear them with a cable sized to the pipe and show you what came out.

In Arlington Heights homes built from the 1940s through the 1960s, the drains are often galvanized steel or cast iron. Both get rough inside with age, and rough pipe catches debris faster. If the same drain keeps clogging, a camera look tells us whether the pipe needs [hydro jetting](/arlington-heights/hydro-jetting) or a repair.
Grease is the main reason kitchen sinks clog. It goes down warm, cools in the pipe and sticks to the walls, and food scraps and soap get caught in it until the water stops moving.

If the other side of a double sink fills up or the dishwasher drains into the sink, the clog is past the trap. We clear the line all the way to the stack and check the trap and arm for leaks. If the disposal is part of the problem, see [garbage disposal repair](/arlington-heights/garbage-disposal-installation-repair).

blocks.h2: Why Drains Clog in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: About 3 in 4 homes in Arlington Heights were built between 1940 and 1989. Age and pipe material play a big role in how drains clog here.

items.h3: Galvanized Drain Lines in Older Homes
items.body: Some postwar homes still have galvanized steel drain lines under sinks and in walls. They rust and close up from the inside, so clogs come back faster.
Years of laundry lint settle in the floor drain and the line below it. When the washer empties, the water has nowhere to go but up.
If several drains slow down together, roots in the clay lateral are a likely cause. That's [sewer drain clearing](#sewer-drain-clearing).

bodies: When every drain slows down at once or water comes up through the basement floor drain, the clog is in the main sewer drain. Clearing it takes a machine that can run the full line from the cleanout to the city main.

We clear the line, then camera it so you can see the cause. In Arlington Heights, the most common causes are roots at clay joints and scale in old cast iron. Repeat clogs get a plan: [sewer rodding](/arlington-heights/sewer-rodding) once a year, [hydro jetting](/arlington-heights/hydro-jetting) or a [sewer repair](/arlington-heights/sewer-repair).

blocks.h2: Drain Cleaning Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Only one drain is slow. Is it the main line?
items.preview: Probably not. One slow fixture is usually a local clog.
items.answer: Probably not. If only one sink, tub or toilet is slow and everything else drains fine, the clog is usually in that fixture's line. If several drains or the floor drain are involved, it's the main line.

items.q: Are chemical drain cleaners safe for older pipes?
items.preview: We don't recommend them, especially on old galvanized or cast iron.
items.answer: We don't recommend them. Harsh chemicals can damage older galvanized and cast iron pipes and rarely clear the whole clog. A cable or jetting removes it without hurting the pipe.

items.q: Why does my kitchen sink keep clogging?
items.preview: Grease buildup in the line. Clearing the whole pipe keeps it from coming back.
items.answer: Usually grease. It builds up in layers along the pipe, so a plunger or a quick snake only opens a small path. Cleaning the full line, and keeping grease out of the sink, stops the cycle.

items.q: When should I call a plumber for a clog?
items.preview: When plunging fails, the clog keeps coming back or several drains are slow.
items.answer: When a plunger doesn't clear it, the clog keeps coming back or more than one drain is slow at the same time. Those signs mean the problem is past what a store-bought fix can handle.

items.q: How much does drain cleaning cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on where the clog is and what caused it. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the clog is, how far down the line and what's causing it. A bathroom sink is a different job than a main line. You get a flat price before any work begins.
